For stable production configurations, pin the scikit-learn dependency version.

docs.title: Quick registry inspection
docs.text:
A useful diagnostic script is:

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    LocalModelFactory,
)

print("Categories:")
print(
    LocalModelFactory.available_categories()
)

print("\nRegression:")
print(
    LocalModelFactory.available_by_category(
        "regression"
    )
)

print("\nClassification:")
print(
    LocalModelFactory.available_by_category(
        "classification"
    )
)

docs.title: Inspect one registration
docs.text:
name = "random_forest_regressor"

print(
    LocalModelFactory.info(name)
)

and:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.supports(
        name,
        "regression",
    )
)

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Component Role BaseLocalModel abstract local-estimator interface LocalModelFactory name/category registry SklearnLocalModel scikit-learn adapter register_all_sklearn_models() dynamic estimator registration clean_sklearn_name() converts sklearn class names to registry names MeanRegressor explicitly registered local mean baseline

docs.title: Important current-source behaviors
docs.text: Behavior Current implementation sklearn estimator discovery dynamic via all_estimators() task classification ClassifierMixin / RegressorMixin estimator naming snake-case class names unsupported sklearn kwargs silently filtered top-level random_state injected by F-Step unsupported random_state on sklearn class filtered by adapter pre-instantiated local model reused, not cloned local model type per cluster one shared configuration for all clusters local predict_proba() supported by adapter when underlying model supports it F-Step predict_proba() not currently implemented mean_regressor alias mean_regressor, dummy_mean mean_regressor through F-Step currently affected by random_state constructor mismatch

docs.title: Mental model
docs.text:
The estimator registry answers “what model should each cluster use?”; the F-Step answers “which fitted instance should handle this observation?”

\[ \boxed{ \text{registered estimator name} \rightarrow \text{new local model per cluster} \rightarrow \text{cluster-specific fit} \rightarrow \text{F-Step prediction} } \]

docs.title: Custom Estimators
docs.text:
You can extend the KFC F-Step with your own local regression or classification models.

The extension point is:

BaseLocalModel

together with:

LocalModelFactory

A custom local estimator participates in the same F-Step workflow as built-in and dynamically registered scikit-learn estimators:

\[ \boxed{ \text{cluster data} \rightarrow \text{custom local model} \rightarrow \text{F-Step prediction matrix} } \]

The relevant source modules are:

kfc_procedure/core/ml/base.py
kfc_procedure/core/ml/sklearn.py
kfc_procedure/core/steps/fstep.py
kfc_procedure/factory/base.py

docs.title: Two ways to use a custom estimator
docs.text:
There are two supported patterns:

  1. register a custom model by name and let F-Step create one instance per cluster;
  2. pass a pre-instantiated model object directly.

The first approach is usually safer because F-Step creates a new registered model for every divergence/cluster pair.

docs.title: Option 1 — Register a custom model
docs.text:
A custom estimator should subclass:

BaseLocalModel

and implement:

fit()
predict()

For classification, you may also implement:

predict_proba()

although the current F-Step itself does not yet expose a probability-prediction method.

docs.title: Minimal custom regressor
docs.text:
import numpy as np

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "median_regressor",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class MedianRegressor(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(
        self,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.random_state = random_state

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.value_ = float(
            np.median(y)
        )

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return np.full(
            len(X),
            self.value_,
            dtype=float,
        )

After registration:

from kfc_procedure import KFCRegressor

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="median_regressor",
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    n_clusters=3,
    random_state=42,
)

model.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train,
)

y_pred = model.predict(
    X_test
)

docs.title: Why random_state should usually be accepted
docs.text:
When F-Step resolves a model by string, it runs:

params = dict(
    self.local_model_params
)

if "random_state" not in params:
    params["random_state"] = self.random_state

and then:

LocalModelFactory.create(
    name,
    **params,
)

Therefore a directly registered custom estimator normally needs to accept:

random_state=None

unless you deliberately design another mechanism that accepts arbitrary keywords.

A constructor such as:

def __init__(
    self,
    random_state=None,
):
    ...

is the simplest compatible pattern.

docs.title: What happens if random_state is missing?
docs.text:
This class:

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "bad_regressor",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class BadRegressor(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(self):
        ...

can be created by the factory directly without extra parameters, but F-Step attempts to call it with:

BadRegressor(
    random_state=...
)

because random_state is injected before factory creation.

Since BaseFactory.create() forwards keyword arguments directly to the registered target, normal Python constructor validation applies.

The result can be:

TypeError:
BadRegressor.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'random_state'

Important

Directly registered custom estimators do not receive the unsupported keyword filtering used by SklearnLocalModel.

docs.title: Custom regressor with parameters
docs.text:
You can expose arbitrary constructor parameters and pass them through local_model_params.

import numpy as np

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "shrunk_mean_regressor",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class ShrunkMeanRegressor(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(
        self,
        shrinkage=0.5,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.shrinkage = shrinkage
        self.random_state = random_state

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.mean_ = float(
            np.mean(y)
        )

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return np.full(
            len(X),
            self.shrinkage * self.mean_,
            dtype=float,
        )

Use it as:

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="shrunk_mean_regressor",
    local_model_params={
        "shrinkage": 0.8,
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    random_state=42,
)

F-Step creates every cluster-local instance with the equivalent of:

ShrunkMeanRegressor(
    shrinkage=0.8,
    random_state=42,
)

unless random_state is already included in local_model_params.

docs.title: Custom classifier
docs.text:
A custom classifier follows the same base interface.

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "local_majority_classifier",
    categories={"classification"},
)
class LocalMajorityClassifier(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(
        self,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.random_state = random_state

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        counts = Counter(y)

        self.class_ = counts.most_common(
            1
        )[0][0]

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return np.full(
            len(X),
            self.class_,
            dtype=object,
        )

Then:

from kfc_procedure import KFCClassifier

model = KFCClassifier(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="local_majority_classifier",
    combiner="combined_classifier",
    random_state=42,
)

model.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train,
)

y_pred = model.predict(
    X_test
)

docs.title: Task categories
docs.text:
The factory uses categories to determine whether an estimator is valid for the current F-Step task.

A regression model should register with:

categories={"regression"}

A classifier should register with:

categories={"classification"}

The base factory also supports multiple categories.

For example:

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "my_multitask_model",
    categories={
        "regression",
        "classification",
    },
)
class MyMultitaskModel(BaseLocalModel):
    ...

Then:

LocalModelFactory.supports(
    "my_multitask_model",
    "regression",
)

and:

LocalModelFactory.supports(
    "my_multitask_model",
    "classification",
)

both return True.

docs.title: How F-Step validates a custom model
docs.text:
For string-based models, F-Step checks:

LocalModelFactory.contains(
    name
)

then:

LocalModelFactory.supports(
    name,
    self.task,
)

before creating the estimator.

Therefore a custom regressor registered only under:

regression

cannot accidentally be selected by KFCClassifier.

docs.title: Check your registration
docs.text:
After registering:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.contains(
        "median_regressor"
    )
)

Expected:

True

Check task support:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.supports(
        "median_regressor",
        "regression",
    )
)

Expected:

True

And:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.supports(
        "median_regressor",
        "classification",
    )
)

Expected:

False

docs.title: Inspect registration metadata
docs.text:
Use:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.info(
        "median_regressor"
    )
)

The factory returns a dictionary containing:

name
class
module
categories
metadata

docs.title: Multiple aliases
docs.text:
A custom model can be registered under several names.

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "median_regressor",
    "median_local",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class MedianRegressor(BaseLocalModel):
    ...

Both names point to the same registered target.

You can inspect aliases with:

LocalModelFactory.find_by_class(
    MedianRegressor
)

docs.title: Name normalization
docs.text:
BaseFactory normalizes registration names by:

  1. requiring strings;
  2. stripping surrounding whitespace;
  3. converting to lowercase;
  4. rejecting empty names.

So:

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "  My_Model  ",
    categories={"regression"},
)

is stored as:

my_model

Factory lookups are normalized in the same way.

docs.title: Duplicate registration protection
docs.text:
The factory rejects duplicate names.

For example, if:

median_regressor

already exists, registering another class under the same normalized name raises a KeyError.

The factory also rejects duplicate names within one registration call.

For example:

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "model",
    "MODEL",
)

normalizes both names to the same key and raises a ValueError.

docs.title: Custom metadata
docs.text:
The registry accepts arbitrary metadata in addition to categories.

For example:

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "median_regressor",
    categories={"regression"},
    author="example",
    version="1.0",
)
class MedianRegressor(BaseLocalModel):
    ...

Inspect it with:

LocalModelFactory.info(
    "median_regressor"
)

The custom values appear under:

metadata

F-Step itself does not currently use arbitrary registration metadata.

docs.title: One instance per cluster
docs.text:
This is one of the main advantages of string registration.

During F-Step fitting, the code runs:

for div_name, cluster_ids in clusters.items():
    for k in np.unique(cluster_ids):
        model = self._resolve()
        model.fit(
            Xc,
            yc,
        )

For a string-based model, _resolve() calls:

LocalModelFactory.create(...)

each time.

Therefore each populated divergence/cluster pair receives a fresh estimator instance.

For example:

Euclidean / cluster 0 -> MedianRegressor instance A
Euclidean / cluster 1 -> MedianRegressor instance B
Euclidean / cluster 2 -> MedianRegressor instance C

GKL / cluster 0       -> MedianRegressor instance D
GKL / cluster 1       -> MedianRegressor instance E
GKL / cluster 2       -> MedianRegressor instance F

Each object is independently fitted.

docs.title: Inspect fitted custom models
docs.text:
After KFC fitting:

for divergence, models in model.fstep_.models_.items():
    print(
        divergence
    )

    for key, metadata in models.items():
        print(
            key,
            metadata["cluster"],
            metadata["model"],
        )

For the registered custom regressor, each:

metadata["model"]

is one fitted custom estimator instance.

docs.title: Scikit-learn-compatible parameter style
docs.text:
Because BaseLocalModel inherits from:

sklearn.base.BaseEstimator

custom estimators work best when constructor parameters are stored as attributes with matching names.

For example:

class MyRegressor(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(
        self,
        scale=1.0,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.scale = scale
        self.random_state = random_state

This follows scikit-learn's estimator conventions and allows inherited parameter introspection behavior to work correctly.

Avoid performing expensive training work in __init__().

Do training in:

fit()

instead.

docs.title: Fitted attributes
docs.text:
A useful convention is to use trailing underscores for values learned during fit().

For example:

class MedianRegressor(BaseLocalModel):

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.median_ = float(
            np.median(y)
        )

        return self

This matches the fitted-attribute style already used throughout the package:

models_
cluster_centers_
labels_
inertia_
strategy_

docs.title: Return self from fit()
docs.text:
The built-in local models return:

self

from fit().

Custom models should follow the same pattern:

def fit(
    self,
    X,
    y,
):
    ...
    return self

This matches scikit-learn estimator conventions and the package's local-model API.

docs.title: Prediction shape
docs.text:
The F-Step expects each local model's:

predict(X)

to return one prediction per input row.

For input:

X.shape == (n_samples, n_features)

the normal prediction shape is:

(n_samples,)

F-Step assigns the result into a one-dimensional prediction vector:

pred[idx] = model.predict(
    X[idx]
)

Therefore custom predict() methods should return a one-dimensional vector compatible with that assignment.

docs.title: Regression prediction dtype
docs.text:
The F-Step initializes predictions with:

np.full(
    X.shape[0],
    np.nan,
)

which produces a floating-point array.

This works naturally for numeric regression predictions.

A custom regressor should normally return numeric values.

docs.title: Classification prediction dtype caveat
docs.text:
The same F-Step code initializes classification prediction arrays with:

np.full(
    X.shape[0],
    np.nan,
)

which is initially floating-point.

If a custom classifier returns non-numeric string labels, assigning them into that array can fail because the target array is numeric.

For example:

"class_a"
"class_b"

may not be assignable into the current float prediction buffer.

Current source limitation

The current F-Step prediction buffer is not explicitly created with dtype=object for classification.

Numeric class labels are the safest choice with the current F-Step implementation.

If you need arbitrary string labels, F-Step should be updated to allocate an object-compatible output buffer for classification.

docs.title: Custom predict_proba()
docs.text:
BaseLocalModel defines:

predict_proba(
    X
)

but its default implementation raises:

NotImplementedError

A custom classifier can override it.

Example:

class MyClassifier(BaseLocalModel):

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.classes_ = np.unique(y)
        ...
        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        ...

    def predict_proba(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        ...

The expected probability format should follow the underlying classifier's own convention, typically:

(n_samples, n_classes)

docs.title: Current KFC probability limitation
docs.text:
Even if a custom local classifier implements:

predict_proba()

the current FStep class itself defines only:

fit()
predict()

and does not define:

predict_proba()

Therefore KFCClassifier.predict_proba() cannot currently obtain a probability matrix from F-Step.

Implementing predict_proba() on a custom local model alone is not sufficient to make end-to-end KFC probabilities work in the current source version.

docs.title: Validation inside a custom model
docs.text:
The base interface does not automatically validate:

X shape
y shape
finite values
target type
minimum sample count

for a custom estimator.

A custom model should perform whatever validation it requires in fit() and predict().

For example:

def fit(
    self,
    X,
    y,
):
    X = np.asarray(X)
    y = np.asarray(y)

    if X.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "X must be 2-dimensional"
        )

    if y.ndim != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            "y must be 1-dimensional"
        )

    if len(X) != len(y):
        raise ValueError(
            "X and y have incompatible lengths"
        )

    ...
    return self

docs.title: F-Step wraps ValueError
docs.text:
If a custom model raises:

ValueError

inside its fit() method, F-Step catches it and raises a new message:

[FSTEP ERROR] divergence='...', cluster=... failed.
Reason: ...
Hint: cluster contains invalid label distribution.

The original exception is preserved as the cause.

Therefore use informative ValueError messages in custom estimators.

docs.title: Example custom validation error
docs.text:
def fit(
    self,
    X,
    y,
):
    if len(y) < 3:
        raise ValueError(
            "At least 3 cluster samples are required."
        )

    ...

F-Step will report the relevant divergence and cluster along with that reason.

docs.title: Option 2 — Pass an estimator object directly
docs.text:
F-Step accepts:

local_model=<object>

when the object is not a string.

For example:

custom = MedianRegressor(
    random_state=42
)

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model=custom,
    combiner="gradientcobra",
)

However, the current _resolve() implementation simply returns:

self.local_model

for every cluster.

It does not clone the object.

docs.title: Important object-reuse behavior
docs.text:
With a direct object:

cluster 0 -> custom.fit(...)
cluster 1 -> same custom.fit(...)
cluster 2 -> same custom.fit(...)

The metadata for multiple clusters can therefore reference the same object after repeated fitting.

The final object state corresponds to the latest fit.

Prefer registry-based custom models

For custom local estimators that need independent fitted state per cluster, register the estimator and pass its string name.

Direct model objects are reused, not cloned, in the current F-Step implementation.

docs.title: If you need to wrap an existing estimator
docs.text:
Suppose you already have a third-party estimator class with:

fit()
predict()

but it does not inherit BaseLocalModel.

A straightforward approach is to write a thin adapter.

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "external_regressor",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class ExternalRegressorAdapter(
    BaseLocalModel
):

    def __init__(
        self,
        alpha=1.0,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.random_state = random_state

        self.model = ExternalRegressor(
            alpha=alpha,
            random_state=random_state,
        )

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.model.fit(
            X,
            y,
        )

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return self.model.predict(
            X
        )

This makes the external estimator compatible with the F-Step registry and cluster-specific instantiation.

docs.title: Wrapping a scikit-learn estimator manually
docs.text:
Normally this is unnecessary because the package auto-registers scikit-learn regressors and classifiers.

If you need a specialized wrapper, you can still create one.

from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "my_ridge",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class MyRidge(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(
        self,
        alpha=1.0,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.alpha = alpha
        self.random_state = random_state

        self.model = Ridge(
            alpha=alpha,
        )

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.model.fit(
            X,
            y,
        )

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return self.model.predict(
            X
        )

docs.title: When manual wrapping is useful
docs.text:
A custom wrapper is useful when you need behavior that the generic SklearnLocalModel adapter does not provide, such as:

special preprocessing
custom validation
custom prediction transformation
extra fitted diagnostics
third-party estimator integration
special constructor mapping

docs.title: Registering builder functions
docs.text:
The factory's registration decorator stores the decorated target and BaseFactory.create() later calls it with constructor arguments.

The package itself uses this pattern for dynamic scikit-learn registration:

def builder(
    model_cls=cls,
    **kwargs,
):
    return SklearnLocalModel(
        model_cls,
        **kwargs,
    )

LocalModelFactory.register(
    key,
    categories={category},
)(builder)

This means a registered target does not have to be a conventional class in practice; it must be callable with the arguments supplied by BaseFactory.create().

For ordinary custom extensions, registering a class is simpler and clearer.

docs.title: Inspect all custom models
docs.text:
You can list the complete registry:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.available()
)

Or only regression models:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.available_by_category(
        "regression"
    )
)

Or classifiers:

print(
    LocalModelFactory.available_by_category(
        "classification"
    )
)

Your custom registration should appear in the relevant list.

docs.title: Factory lifecycle helpers
docs.text:
Because LocalModelFactory inherits BaseFactory, it also exposes registry management methods.

These include:

unregister(name)
clear()

For example:

LocalModelFactory.unregister(
    "median_regressor"
)

removes only that registration name.

Warning

clear() removes all entries from the current LocalModelFactory registry.

This includes dynamically registered scikit-learn models and package built-ins in the current process.

It is mainly useful for controlled testing, not ordinary application use.

docs.title: Re-registering after clear()
docs.text:
The package's scikit-learn registration is triggered when:

kfc_procedure.core.ml

is imported.

If you manually clear the registry later, simply importing an already imported module again does not necessarily rerun the module-level registration code.

For tests that manipulate the registry, explicitly manage restoration rather than relying on normal import caching.

docs.title: Testing a custom estimator before KFC
docs.text:
A useful development pattern is to test the factory and estimator directly.

local = LocalModelFactory.create(
    "median_regressor",
    random_state=42,
)

local.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train,
)

prediction = local.predict(
    X_test
)

print(
    prediction.shape
)

Only after that succeeds should you insert it into the full KFC pipeline.

docs.title: Test task metadata
docs.text:
assert LocalModelFactory.contains(
    "median_regressor"
)

assert LocalModelFactory.supports(
    "median_regressor",
    "regression",
)

assert not LocalModelFactory.supports(
    "median_regressor",
    "classification",
)

docs.title: Test independent F-Step instances
docs.text:
To verify that string registration creates separate cluster models:

models = model.fstep_.models_[
    "euclidean"
]

instances = [
    metadata["model"]
    for metadata
    in models.values()
]

print(
    [
        id(instance)
        for instance
        in instances
    ]
)

For a string-registered custom model, the IDs should normally be distinct.

docs.title: Custom estimator with learned coefficients
docs.text:
A more realistic example:

import numpy as np

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "least_squares_local",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class LeastSquaresLocal(
    BaseLocalModel
):

    def __init__(
        self,
        fit_intercept=True,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.fit_intercept = fit_intercept
        self.random_state = random_state

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        X = np.asarray(
            X,
            dtype=float,
        )

        y = np.asarray(
            y,
            dtype=float,
        )

        if self.fit_intercept:
            X_design = np.column_stack(
                [
                    np.ones(len(X)),
                    X,
                ]
            )
        else:
            X_design = X

        coef, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(
            X_design,
            y,
            rcond=None,
        )

        if self.fit_intercept:
            self.intercept_ = coef[0]
            self.coef_ = coef[1:]
        else:
            self.intercept_ = 0.0
            self.coef_ = coef

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        X = np.asarray(
            X,
            dtype=float,
        )

        return (
            X @ self.coef_
            + self.intercept_
        )

Then:

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="least_squares_local",
    local_model_params={
        "fit_intercept": True,
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    n_clusters=3,
    random_state=42,
)

docs.title: Inspect custom fitted attributes
docs.text:
After fitting:

local = model.fstep_.models_[
    "euclidean"
]["m0"]["model"]

print(
    local.coef_
)

print(
    local.intercept_
)

Because KFC stores the actual fitted local object, all custom fitted attributes remain accessible.

docs.title: Custom classifier with probabilities
docs.text:
A simple illustration:

import numpy as np

from kfc_procedure.core.ml import (
    BaseLocalModel,
    LocalModelFactory,
)


@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "prior_classifier",
    categories={"classification"},
)
class PriorClassifier(
    BaseLocalModel
):

    def __init__(
        self,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        self.random_state = random_state

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        self.classes_, counts = np.unique(
            y,
            return_counts=True,
        )

        self.probabilities_ = (
            counts
            / counts.sum()
        )

        self.majority_ = self.classes_[
            np.argmax(
                self.probabilities_
            )
        ]

        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return np.full(
            len(X),
            self.majority_,
        )

    def predict_proba(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        return np.tile(
            self.probabilities_,
            (
                len(X),
                1,
            ),
        )

This local estimator itself supports probabilities.

However, as noted earlier, the current F-Step does not yet aggregate local probabilities.

docs.title: Designing for small clusters
docs.text:
Custom estimators should account for the fact that F-Step trains on local subsets.

A cluster may contain very few observations.

Possible strategies include:

validate minimum sample count
fall back to a simple constant predictor
regularize aggressively
support one-class classification where meaningful
raise an informative ValueError

The package does not impose one fallback policy for custom estimators.

docs.title: Example minimum-size check
docs.text:
def fit(
    self,
    X,
    y,
):
    if len(y) < 5:
        raise ValueError(
            "This local model requires at least 5 samples."
        )

    ...

F-Step will add divergence and cluster context to the error.

docs.title: Do not depend on cluster ID in the estimator constructor
docs.text:
The current F-Step does not pass:

divergence name
cluster ID

into _resolve().

Those values are only stored in the F-Step metadata after fitting.

So a registered custom estimator constructor receives only:

local_model_params
random_state

unless you explicitly include other keys in local_model_params.

If an estimator needs the current cluster ID or divergence name, F-Step itself must be extended to pass that context.

docs.title: Do not depend on full training data
docs.text:
A custom local model's fit() receives only:

Xc
yc

for one cluster.

It does not automatically receive:

the full X
the full y
other cluster data
K-Step centroids
divergence objects
C-Step state

This is intentional separation between KFC stages.

docs.title: Current custom-estimator limitations
docs.text: Capability Current behavior registered custom class supported custom regression category supported custom classification category supported multiple aliases supported custom registration metadata supported independent model per cluster by string name supported custom constructor parameters supported top-level random_state injected automatically unsupported custom kwargs filtered No direct object cloning No different custom model per divergence No different custom model per cluster No fit-time kwargs No cluster ID passed to constructor No divergence passed to constructor No F-Step probability aggregation No arbitrary string-label-safe prediction buffer not guaranteed in current F-Step

docs.title: Recommended extension pattern
docs.text:
For the current source version, the most robust pattern is:

@LocalModelFactory.register(
    "my_estimator",
    categories={"regression"},
)
class MyEstimator(BaseLocalModel):

    def __init__(
        self,
        ...,
        random_state=None,
    ):
        # store constructor arguments
        ...

    def fit(
        self,
        X,
        y,
    ):
        # validate and learn fitted state
        ...
        return self

    def predict(
        self,
        X,
    ):
        # return one value per row
        ...

Then use:

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="my_estimator",
    local_model_params={
        # constructor parameters
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    random_state=42,
)

This ensures F-Step creates a fresh estimator for each cluster.

docs.title: 1. Check registration
docs.text:
print(
    LocalModelFactory.contains(
        "my_estimator"
    )
)

docs.title: 2. Check category
docs.text:
print(
    LocalModelFactory.supports(
        "my_estimator",
        "regression",
    )
)

docs.title: 3. Create it directly
docs.text:
local = LocalModelFactory.create(
    "my_estimator",
    random_state=42,
)

If this fails, fix the constructor before testing KFC.

docs.title: 4. Fit directly
docs.text:
local.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train,
)

docs.title: 5. Check prediction shape
docs.text:
pred = local.predict(
    X_test
)

print(
    np.asarray(
        pred
    ).shape
)

Expected:

(n_samples,)

docs.title: 6. Fit KFC
docs.text:
model.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train,
)

If a cluster fit fails, inspect the Reason: field inside the F-Step error.

docs.title: 7. Inspect each fitted instance
docs.text:
for divergence, models in model.fstep_.models_.items():
    for name, metadata in models.items():
        print(
            divergence,
            name,
            metadata["cluster"],
            metadata["model"],
        )

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Component Purpose BaseLocalModel custom local-estimator interface LocalModelFactory.register() register estimator names and categories LocalModelFactory.create() create new registered instances LocalModelFactory.supports() validate task category LocalModelFactory.info() inspect registration FStep._resolve() creates string-based models or reuses object models local_model_params constructor parameters random_state injected by F-Step when absent

docs.title: Mental model
docs.text:
A custom F-Step estimator should be a small, independent supervised model that can be constructed repeatedly and fitted on one cluster at a time.

\[ \boxed{ \text{register class} \rightarrow \text{factory creates one model per cluster} \rightarrow \text{fit on local subset} \rightarrow \text{predict one F-Step column} } \]

docs.title: Estimator Parameters
docs.text:
This guide explains how parameters are passed from KFCRegressor and KFCClassifier to the local estimators fitted by the F-Step.

The main user-facing argument is:

local_model_params

For example:

from kfc_procedure import KFCRegressor

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="ridge",
    local_model_params={
        "alpha": 2.0,
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    random_state=42,
)

The F-Step uses the same local-model configuration for every divergence/cluster pair.

docs.title: Parameter flow
docs.text:
The parameter path is:

KFCRegressor / KFCClassifier
            │
            ▼
local_model_params
            │
            ▼
FStep
            │
            ▼
LocalModelFactory
            │
            ▼
SklearnLocalModel
            │
            ▼
scikit-learn estimator constructor

For a string-based local model, the current F-Step resolves parameters using:

params = dict(
    self.local_model_params
)

if "random_state" not in params:
    params["random_state"] = self.random_state

return LocalModelFactory.create(
    name,
    **params,
)

So the top-level KFC random_state is added automatically unless you provide a model-specific value.

docs.title: Basic usage
docs.text:
Regression:

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="ridge",
    local_model_params={
        "alpha": 1.5,
        "fit_intercept": True,
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    random_state=42,
)

Classification:

from kfc_procedure import KFCClassifier

model = KFCClassifier(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="logistic_regression",
    local_model_params={
        "C": 1.0,
        "max_iter": 1000,
        "class_weight": "balanced",
    },
    combiner="combined_classifier",
    random_state=42,
)

docs.title: The same parameters are used in every cluster
docs.text:
The current F-Step has one global:

local_model

and one global:

local_model_params

Therefore:

local_model="ridge"

local_model_params={
    "alpha": 2.0,
}

means:

Euclidean / cluster 0 -> Ridge(alpha=2.0)
Euclidean / cluster 1 -> Ridge(alpha=2.0)
Euclidean / cluster 2 -> Ridge(alpha=2.0)

GKL / cluster 0       -> Ridge(alpha=2.0)
GKL / cluster 1       -> Ridge(alpha=2.0)
GKL / cluster 2       -> Ridge(alpha=2.0)

The current F-Step does not provide separate parameter dictionaries per divergence or per cluster.

docs.title: How scikit-learn parameters are filtered
docs.text:
Dynamically registered scikit-learn estimators are wrapped by:

SklearnLocalModel

The adapter inspects the estimator constructor with:

inspect.signature(
    model_cls.__init__
)

and keeps only keyword arguments whose names appear in that signature:

valid_kwargs = {
    key: value
    for key, value in kwargs.items()
    if key in sig.parameters
}

Then it constructs:

self.model = model_cls(
    **valid_kwargs
)

This behavior applies to estimators discovered through sklearn.utils.all_estimators().

docs.title: Unsupported parameters are silently dropped
docs.text:
Consider:

local_model="ridge"

local_model_params={
    "alpha": 2.0,
    "not_a_parameter": 123,
}

If Ridge.__init__() does not contain:

not_a_parameter

then the adapter simply removes it.

The estimator is effectively constructed with:

Ridge(
    alpha=2.0,
)

Typos can be silent

Because unsupported scikit-learn constructor keywords are filtered out, a misspelled parameter may not raise an error.

For example:

local_model_params={
    "n_estimator": 300,
}

can be silently ignored when the estimator actually expects:

n_estimators

Inspect the fitted estimator when parameter correctness matters.

docs.title: Inspect the effective parameters
docs.text:
After fitting, retrieve one local estimator:

local_model = model.fstep_.models_[
    "euclidean"
]["m0"]["model"]

For a SklearnLocalModel, call:

print(
    local_model.get_params()
)

The adapter delegates this call to the underlying scikit-learn estimator:

return self.model.get_params(
    deep=deep
)

This is the simplest way to confirm which parameters were actually accepted.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="random_forest_regressor",
    local_model_params={
        "n_estimators": 300,
        "max_depth": 8,
        "not_real": 999,
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    random_state=42,
)

model.fit(
    X_train,
    y_train,
)

local_model = model.fstep_.models_[
    "euclidean"
]["m0"]["model"]

params = local_model.get_params()

print(
    params["n_estimators"]
)

print(
    params["max_depth"]
)

print(
    "not_real" in params
)

Expected behavior:

300
8
False

docs.title: Access the underlying estimator
docs.text:
For dynamically registered scikit-learn models, the wrapper stores the real estimator on:

local_model.model

Example:

wrapped = model.fstep_.models_[
    "euclidean"
]["m0"]["model"]

print(
    wrapped.model
)

This is useful when you want estimator-specific fitted attributes such as:

wrapped.model.coef_
wrapped.model.feature_importances_
wrapped.model.classes_

depending on the selected estimator.

docs.title: random_state
docs.text:
The F-Step automatically adds:

random_state=self.random_state

when the local parameter dictionary does not already contain that key.

So:

model = KFCRegressor(
    ...,
    random_state=42,
)

attempts to configure every string-based local model with:

random_state=42

docs.title: If the estimator supports random_state
docs.text:
For example:

local_model="random_forest_regressor"

with:

random_state=42

is effectively constructed with:

RandomForestRegressor(
    random_state=42,
    ...
)

assuming you did not provide another value in local_model_params.

docs.title: If the estimator does not support random_state
docs.text:
For dynamically wrapped scikit-learn estimators, the adapter filters the unsupported keyword out.

For example, if the selected estimator constructor has no random_state parameter, this injected value is removed before construction.

This means the top-level KFC seed can be forwarded broadly without breaking most dynamically registered scikit-learn models.

docs.title: Override the top-level seed
docs.text:
A value supplied directly through:

local_model_params

takes precedence.

model = KFCRegressor(
    divergences=["euclidean"],
    local_model="random_forest_regressor",
    local_model_params={
        "n_estimators": 300,
        "random_state": 123,
    },
    combiner="gradientcobra",
    random_state=42,
)

Here the local forests receive:

random_state=123

rather than:

42

because F-Step only injects its value when the key is absent.

    "C": 1.0,
    "kernel": "rbf",
    "probability": True,
